Subject: Apollo Systems — private deployment orchestration and networking runbook

Hi Tim + Sophie,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. To keep momentum I wanted to kick off the written runbook path for the private deployment and surface a small set of items we need to confirm before we lock the installation window. Attaching our private-deploy checklist and a blank requirements sheet for your network team.

High level asks (can you reply inline):
- Preferred model: VPC peering to RDW VPC + Private Link for control-plane endpoints, or IPsec VPN? If you have a procurement constraint that forces VPN-only, flag that.
- VPC CIDR(s) for the two clusters we plan to peer (management vs. inference). If CIDRs overlap we will propose a NAT/Gateway translation approach.
- Firewall/NGFW owners and expected egress port list. We will need ports TCP 443, 10250, 9090 (agent/metrics) opened to our peered CIDR.
- On-prem package deployment: do you provision a dedicated outbound NAT IP for the appliance to register, or will the appliance sit behind a corporate proxy?

Proposed near-term calendar: we can schedule the technical kickoff with infra+networking on Monday 24 May at 10am PT. If that works we will circulate an agenda and invite links.

Attachments: rdw_private_deploy_checklist.pdf (checklist), apollosys_vpc_requirements.xlsx (blank template).

Next steps for us: Vivek will draft a short network design doc with fallback options (peering vs VPN) and Hannah will enumerate the SOC2/audit artifacts you asked about.

Thanks — looking forward to the details so we can confirm the install runway.

Best,
Monica Patel

Monica — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from our side (I'll ask our network lead to confirm the Excel):

- Preferred approach: VPC peering between our app VPC and Redwood's inference VPC. We prefer not to introduce an IPsec tunnel unless absolutely necessary.
- Tentative CIDRs: app-vpc: 10.10.0.0/16, infra-management: 10.20.0.0/24. I believe there are no overlaps with public cloud ranges you supplied but I'll validate.
- Firewall owners: Network team (cc-ing Sophie). We'll need a full port list for the appliance; opening 443 is fine as long as we can control source IPs.
- On-prem packaging: The appliance will run in our colo cage and will have a dedicated outbound NAT IP. No corporate proxy in front of the appliance.

Also: procurement will need SOC2 artifacts (scope, SOC2 report, and a short data flow diagram) before we sign the final SOW.

I can do the Monday slot. If we need to move that to morning ET, let me know.

Thanks,
Tim

Thanks Monica — looping in Laura for scheduling notes. Quick technical summary and recommended default design based on Tim's answers:

Proposal (default):
- Use VPC peering between Apollo app VPC (10.10.0.0/16) and Redwood inference VPC. Peering for data path; PrivateLink endpoints for control/telemetry to avoid asymmetric routing.
- Because management/agent traffic will come from a dedicated NAT IP at Apollo, we will whitelist that NAT IP on our egress ACLs.
- If any CIDR overlap shows up, we will do SNAT on the appliance egress at Apollo side (we have a small NAT shim in the on-prem package that handles 1:1 translation).
- Ports: outbound TCP 443 for control plane; TCP 10250 for node agent diagnostics if you want direct connectivity; TCP 9090 optional for metrics forwarding. We'll provide an explicit list in the final runbook.
- Certificate provisioning: we will use mTLS for the agent registration handshake; please confirm whether your internal PKI can accommodate a Redwood-submitted CSR or if you prefer to use a wildcard cert.

Safeguards / fallback:
- Fallback to site-to-site IPSec VPN if peering is disallowed by your security team. We can orchestrate a short-lived VPN for cutover.
- Staged rollout: start with a single inference zone, validate model performance and telemetry, then expand.

I attached our latest private-deploy checklist for internal review. Monica, can you confirm we should capture the agent NAT IP in the SOW? Also Hannah — can you start a brief SOC2 artifact checklist we can send to procurement?

-Vivek
